Simulation-based item-restscore cutoffs

Source: R/item_restscore_cutoff.R
RMitemRestscoreCutoff.Rd

Simulates datasets from a Rasch or partial credit model that fits and resembles your data, and computes each item's observed minus expected item-restscore gamma (Kreiner, 2011) in each. Passed to RMitemRestscore(), the result gives bootstrap p-values corrected across items, and an interval per item that describes where a fitting item's difference is expected to fall.

Usage

RMitemRestscoreCutoff(
  data,
  iterations = 400,
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  cutoff_method = "hdci",
  hdci_width = 0.95,
  dgp = c("conditional", "resample")
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Only complete cases (rows without NA) are used.

iterations

Integer. Number of simulated datasets. Default 400. Use 1000 or more for a final analysis (see Reproducibility in RMitemRestscore()).

parallel

Logical. Run the simulations in parallel via mirai when it is installed. Default TRUE.

n_cores

Integer or NULL. Number of parallel workers. When NULL, getOption("mc.cores") is used. If that is unset too, a warning is given and the simulations run sequentially.

verbose

Logical. Show a progress bar. Default FALSE.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. See easyRasch2-reproducibility for what this guarantees and how it interacts with parallel.

cutoff_method

Character. How the interval per item is computed: "hdci" (default), the highest-density continuous interval from ggdist::hdci() (needs ggdist), or "quantile", the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles.

hdci_width

Numeric. Width of the interval with cutoff_method = "hdci". Default 0.95. Ignored with "quantile".

The interval describes where a fitting item's difference is expected to fall. It is not a decision rule. Flagging every item outside a width-w interval tests all k items at once, with a family-wise error rate of 1 - w^k. Decisions come from the corrected p-value in RMitemRestscore(), as shown for infit in Johansson (2026).

dgp

Character. How datasets are simulated. "conditional" (default) simulates each respondent's response pattern from the model given their observed total score, with the item parameters fixed (a conditional null). The expected gamma is computed from the observed score distribution, which the conditional null keeps. "resample" draws person locations from the WLE estimates with replacement and simulates responses from the model (a marginal null). With the Rasch model true, pooled over four designs, the family-wise rate with correction = "fwer" was 5.0% with the conditional null and 6.4% with the resample null. The conditional null takes about 1.2 to 1.6 times as long. Experimental.

Value

A list with:

results

data.frame with the columns iteration, Item, Observed, Expected and Difference, one row per item and simulated dataset. Difference is Observed - Expected, the statistic RMitemRestscore() tests.

item_cutoffs

data.frame with the interval per item: Item, diff_low, diff_high, computed by cutoff_method.

actual_iterations

Number of simulated datasets that could be used. Everything downstream rests on this rather than on iterations, so it is the number to report.

requested_iterations

The iterations argument, so that callers can tell how many simulated datasets were left out.

sample_n

Number of complete cases used.

sample_n_total

Number of respondents in data, before the complete-case filter.

sample_has_na

Logical. Whether data contained missing values.

sample_summary

Summary of the WLE person locations.

item_names

Item names from data.

cutoff_method

"hdci" or "quantile".

hdci_width

The HDCI width (used only with "hdci").

dgp

"conditional" or "resample".

Details

Why simulate. The asymptotic test in iarm::item_restscore() divides the observed minus expected gamma by the standard error of the observed gamma alone. The expected gamma is estimated from the same data and correlates with the observed one, so that standard error is too large for the difference, and the difference is also biased upwards in small samples. With the Rasch model true, the test is liberal for dichotomous items in small or mistargeted samples and conservative for polytomous items, and it flags too few underfitting items in every case. The simulated reference distribution replaces the asymptotic one and absorbs both problems. The simulation study of the asymptotic test is reported at https://pgmj.github.io/rasch_book/chapters/restscore-asymptotic-null.html.

Simulation. The generating model has the CML item parameters (psychotools) and the WLE person locations of data. In each iteration a dataset is simulated by dgp, the model is refitted by CML (psychotools::pcmodel()), and the observed and expected gamma are computed as in iarm::item_restscore(), by a faster internal routine that skips the standard errors and the rounding of the printed values. The refit matters. The expected gamma varies from sample to sample because the thresholds do, and holding them fixed would reproduce the problem the simulation is meant to solve. A simulated dataset that cannot be refitted, for example because a response category is empty, is left out, and RMitemRestscore() reports how many in its caption.

Parallel processing needs the optional mirai package. The iarm package must be installed (it is in Suggests).

References

Johansson, M. (2026). Simulation-based cutoffs for conditional item fit in Rasch models: Iterations, multiplicity correction, and decision stability. PsyArXiv. doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2

Kreiner, S. (2011). A Note on Item-Restscore Association in Rasch Models. Applied Psychological Measurement, 35(7), 557-561. doi:10.1177/0146621611410227

See also

RMitemRestscore() for the test, RMitemRestscorePlot() to plot the simulated values.

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("iarm", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(42)
  sim_data <- as.data.frame(
    matrix(sample(0:1, 200 * 10, replace = TRUE), nrow = 200, ncol = 10)
  )
  colnames(sim_data) <- paste0("Item", 1:10)

  # Run 100 iterations sequentially for a quick demo
  cutoff_res <- RMitemRestscoreCutoff(sim_data, iterations = 100,
                                      parallel = FALSE, seed = 42)
  cutoff_res$item_cutoffs

  # Flag on bootstrap p-values in RMitemRestscore()
  RMitemRestscore(sim_data, cutoff = cutoff_res)
}
#> Bootstrap p-values are based on 100 iterations, below the recommended 400.
#> ℹ The family-wise error rate is controlled at any number of iterations. With few iterations the p-values are coarse, and which comparisons get flagged depends on the seed.
#> ℹ See Johansson (2026), doi:10.31234/osf.io/7pqz4_v2.
#> ℹ Raise `iterations` in RMitemRestscoreCutoff().

#> Table: Item-restscore associations. n = 200 respondents. Equal-tailed parametric bootstrap p-values for the difference from 100 iterations, conditional DGP, multiplicity correction: Westfall-Young step-down (FWER). p-values cannot be smaller than 2/(100+1) = 0.02. This is below the recommended 400, where decisions depend on the seed (Johansson, 2026). Flagged (adj. p < 0.05): overfit = observed above expected (over-discrimination, often local dependence); underfit = below (under-discrimination, often multidimensionality/noise).
